chapter: Road life, arranging and racial dangers
title: The sheriff who wanted only Turkey in the Straw
summary: At Palestine, Texas, a sheriff with two pistols danced alone while the band played Turkey in the Straw all night.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Was there much of a feeling among the White people who would go to these dances... Did they feel that the Black music had something that the White music didn't? Did they seem to feel that you were very good at playing?

Yeah, yeah. Not only that, we ran into... There was a dance down here in Palestina... See, we knew how to handle all the (?)s... We still didn't think about that. We watched out for that. And we ...(?). . .(?). . . down there at Palestina.

We went down there the first time, and we played out on kind of like a lawn(?)... A great big band(?), and they had a big lawn, a big (?) spread out there, and people was dancin' on it. The sheriff comes down with two big pistols on, and he wouldn't let nobody dance but himself! In other words, he didn't want nothing but "Turkey In The Straw" all the time. And we had to play "Turkey In The Straw." So Walter Page, he was leading the band... I told Walter, "There's a man who says he don't want us to play nothin' but 'Turkey in the Straw' all the time for him," and wasn't nobody dancing but him, by himself, standing out there with some big boots on, right in the middle of the floor, and the people are all standing... He's a bad man, so wasn't nobody said nothin' to him; all the people were standing around and listening to it!
How long did that go on for?
It went on the whole night while we played!

So the boss man said, "He's the baddest man in this part of the country." So he said, "Go ahead, I'm paying you. Go ahead and play. Don't make no difference. There's nobody gonna dance." He said, "I'm gonna pay you anyhow."
Could you actually play "Turkey In The Straw"?
Yeah! Sure, we played it. Sure. We had to play it! We better play it! Ha-ha.
Sort of cowboy country, is it?
Well, the cowboy country mostly was back out in West Texas. But this here was down in Southeast Texas.
